node.name: .gitignore
node.rich_text:
Let me show you exactly what's in it.## What is `frontend/.gitignore`?
A `.gitignore` file tells **Git what NOT to upload to GitHub**. Any file or folder listed inside it gets completely ignored — Git pretends it doesn't exist.
---
### What it's ignoring and WHY:
#### 🚫 Dependencies ``` /node_modules ← 200MB+ of libraries — recreated with npm install ```
#### 🚫 Next.js build output ``` /.next/ ← compiled code — recreated with npm run dev /out/ ← static export output /build ← production build ```
#### 🚫 Secrets / Environment files ``` .env* ← ALL .env files — contains passwords and tokens (this is why .env.local is never pushed) ```
#### 🚫 Logs ``` npm-debug.log* yarn-debug.log* yarn-error.log* ```
#### 🚫 OS junk files ``` .DS_Store ← Mac folder metadata (useless on Linux/Windows) *.pem ← SSL certificate files ```
#### 🚫 TypeScript generated files ``` *.tsbuildinfo ← TypeScript compiler cache next-env.d.ts ← auto-generated by Next.js ```
---
### What DOES get pushed to GitHub:
``` src/ ✅ your actual code public/ ✅ images and icons package.json ✅ dependency list next.config.ts ✅ Next.js config tsconfig.json ✅ TypeScript config .gitignore ✅ this file itself ```
---
### Simple rule:
``` .gitignore = "don't upload these to GitHub"
Big files → node_modules, .next Secret files → .env, .env.local Generated → *.tsbuildinfo, next-env.d.ts ```
There are **two** `.gitignore` files in your project: - `frontend/.gitignore` — for the frontend only - `/ethiovuln-main/.gitignore` — for the whole project (backend + frontend)
